In Motoi Scheme, show me an example of follow-through: motion continues past the stop.

```motoi
(let* ((ball (world/spawn 50 200))
       (antenna (world/spawn 50 180))
       (stopped #f)
       (sway-vel 0))
  (entity/sprite! ball "circle" 16 "purple")
  (entity/sprite! antenna "circle" 6 "violet")
  
  ;; ball glides to a stop
  (motion/glide-to ball 300 200 90)
  
  ;; after 90 frames, ball has stopped, but antenna keeps swaying
  (world/after 90
    (lambda ()
      (set! stopped #t)
      (set! sway-vel 4.0)))  ;; initial sway velocity
  
  ;; antenna follows ball, then sways when stopped
  (world/after 1
    (lambda ()
      (if stopped
          (let* ((ball-x (entity/x ball))
                 (ball-y (entity/y ball))
                 (ant-x (entity/x antenna))
                 (offset (- ant-x ball-x)))
            ;; sway back and forth with damping
            (set! sway-vel (+ sway-vel (* offset -0.1)))
            (set! sway-vel (* sway-vel 0.95))  ;; damping
            (entity/set-pos! antenna (+ ball-x sway-vel) (- ball-y 20)))
          (let ((ball-x (entity/x ball))
                (ball-y (entity/y ball)))
            (entity/set-pos! antenna ball-x (- ball-y 20))))
      
      (world/after 1 (world/current-callback)))))
```

A ball rolls to a stop. Its antenna continues to sway back and forth, gradually settling.

```motoi
;; A legato voice with vibrato: 6 Hz wobble, ±15 cents depth.
(define vibrato-voice
  (let ((v (voice/create 'vibrato-voice)))
    (voice/waveform v (createPeriodicWave (list 1.0 0.5 0.3 0.15)))
    (voice/envelope v (adsr 0.05 0.1 0.8 0.3))
    (voice/vibrato v 6.0 15.0)  ;; 6 Hz rate, 15 cents depth
    v))

;; Play a sustained A4 for 2 beats.
(note/strike 'A4 'half 0.75 vibrato-voice)
```
Vibrato is a *periodic variation in pitch*—a slight wobble, usually 5–7 Hz (5–7 wobbles per second), ±10–30 cents. It's not an envelope (amplitude over time); it's **pitch modulation**.
In Motoi Scheme, show me an example of sequence — repeating a pattern at different pitch levels.

```motoi
(define (simple-sequence)
  ;; motif 1: C D E
  (note/strike 60 'eighth 0.7)  ; C4
  (note/strike 62 'eighth 0.7)  ; D4
  (note/strike 64 'eighth 0.7)  ; E4
  ;; motif 2: D E F♯ (up one step)
  (note/strike 62 'eighth 0.75) ; D4
  (note/strike 64 'eighth 0.75) ; E4
  (note/strike 66 'eighth 0.75) ; F♯4
  ;; motif 3: E F♯ G♯ (up one more step)
  (note/strike 64 'eighth 0.8)  ; E4
  (note/strike 66 'eighth 0.8)  ; F♯4
  (note/strike 68 'eighth 0.8)) ; G♯4

(simple-sequence)
```

A **sequence** is when you take a short melodic fragment (a *motif*) and repeat it at a *different pitch level*. **Example:** a three-note motif (C D E) repeated one step higher (D E F♯), then one more (E F♯ G♯).

In Motoi Scheme, show me an example of evade: flee from where the threat will be.

```motoi
;; A dot evading a pursuing threat.
(define (evade-demo)
  (let* ((w (world/spawn '()))
         (threat (world/spawn w `((pos (4 4))
                                   (vel (1.0 1.0))
                                   (max-speed 2.0)
                                   (kind threat))))
         (evader (world/spawn w `((pos (16 12))
                                   (vel (0 0))
                                   (max-speed 2.5)
                                   (kind evader)))))
    (ai/max-force! evader 0.7)
    
    (define (draw)
      (clear-cell)
      (let ((tpos (entity/pos threat))
            (epos (entity/pos evader)))
        (paint-cell (car tpos) (cdr tpos) "👹")
        (paint-cell (car epos) (cdr epos) "🕊️")))
    
    (define (step)
      ;; threat seeks evader
      (let ((steer-threat (ai/seek threat (car (entity/pos evader)) (cdr (entity/pos evader)))))
        (entity/accel! threat (car steer-threat) (cdr steer-threat)))
      ;; evader evades threat
      (let ((steer-evade (ai/evade evader threat 10)))
        (entity/accel! evader (car steer-evade) (cdr steer-evade))
        (world/step w)))
    
    (big-bang w
              (on-tick step)
              (to-draw draw))))

(evade-demo)
```
